Gender Inequality Analysis

Tzu-Ting Lu

Research question

How did gender inequality change across countries between 2010 and 2019?

Load packages

library(readr)
library(dplyr)
library(sf)
library(ggplot2)
library(countrycode)

Read and prepare GII data

gii_raw <- read_csv(
  "data/HDR25_Composite_indices_complete_time_series.csv",
  show_col_types = FALSE
)

gii_change <- gii_raw |>
  select(iso3, country, gii_2010, gii_2019) |>
  mutate(
    gii_change = gii_2019 - gii_2010
  )

head(gii_change)
## # A tibble: 6 × 5
##   iso3  country             gii_2010 gii_2019 gii_change
##   <chr> <chr>                  <dbl>    <dbl>      <dbl>
## 1 AFG   Afghanistan            0.704    0.676    -0.0280
## 2 ALB   Albania                0.192    0.131    -0.061 
## 3 DZA   Algeria                0.508    0.385    -0.123 
## 4 AND   Andorra               NA       NA        NA     
## 5 AGO   Angola                 0.556    0.536    -0.0200
## 6 ATG   Antigua and Barbuda   NA       NA        NA

Join world boundaries

world <- st_read(
  "data/world_countries.geojson",
  quiet = TRUE
)

world <- world |>
  mutate(
    iso3 = countrycode(
      ISO,
      origin = "iso2c",
      destination = "iso3c"
    )
  )

world_gii <- world |>
  left_join(
    gii_change,
    by = "iso3",
    na_matches = "never"
  )

Data coverage

world_gii |>
  st_drop_geometry() |>
  summarise(
    total = n(),
    with_change = sum(!is.na(gii_change)),
    missing_change = sum(is.na(gii_change))
  )
##   total with_change missing_change
## 1   251         157             94

Map of GII change

ggplot(world_gii) +
  geom_sf(
    aes(fill = gii_change),
    colour = "white",
    linewidth = 0.1
  ) +
  scale_fill_gradient2(
    low = "#2166AC",
    mid = "white",
    high = "#B2182B",
    midpoint = 0,
    na.value = "grey80",
    name = "GII change\n2019 − 2010"
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Change in Gender Inequality, 2010–2019",
    subtitle = "Blue: decrease | Red: increase | Grey: missing data",
    caption = "Sources: UNDP HDR 2025; Esri World Countries Generalized"
  ) +
  theme_void()

Interpretation

GII change is calculated as the 2019 value minus the 2010 value. Negative values indicate reduced gender inequality, while positive values indicate increased gender inequality.

Of the 251 mapped countries and territories, 157 have a calculated change and 94 have missing values. Grey areas indicate missing data, not zero change.

These differences describe changes over time; they do not explain the causes of those changes.

Sources

  • UNDP Human Development Report data: HDR25 composite indices time series.
  • Esri World Countries Generalized: world boundaries downloaded as GeoJSON.

Of the 94 features without a calculated change, 54 have no matching ISO3 entry in the UNDP table. The remaining 40 match an entry but lack GII data for at least one of the two years. Missing values are retained and shown in grey.
